title: Customer signal consolidation and prioritized onboarding lanes for isolated/private deployments
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem: Sales and Solutions Engineering receive a high volume of private/VPC/on-prem deployment requests with inconsistent signals (email threads, Jira tickets, spreadsheet intake). Engineering capacity is limited; customers with similar networking constraints (air-gapped, strict egress policies, legacy appliance proxies) are being handled ad hoc, causing duplicate effort and slow SLAs.

Objective: Create a consolidated signal model and a set of prioritized onboarding lanes that map customer networking posture and upgrade readiness to a deterministic engagement path (self-serve docs, concierge, or escalated engineering program). The lanes should be actionable, instrumentable in the Console, and produce clear downstream artifacts for Eng (runbooks, compatibility tests, preflight scripts).

Scope: Non-bug customer requests only (feature/ops/onboarding). Focus on networking and upgrade constraints: air-gap, strict outbound-only, NTLM/proxy appliances, limited NAT pools, and scheduled maintenance windows. Excludes license/legal reviews and purely infra procurement issues.

Outcomes: 1) Standardized signal schema (network capabilities + constraints) captured during intake. 2) A three-lane prioritization fabric: Self-Serve, Concierge (SE-led), and Escalation (Eng+PM program). 3) Automation hooks: preflight probe results, templated remediation steps, and a dashboard showing runway and expected lead time per lane.
acceptance_criteria: A JSON schema for 'private_deploy_signal' that covers networking, upgrade constraints, and critical dependencies is drafted and reviewed by SE and SRE.
Intake form prototype (Docs + automateable API) implemented and validated with 3 pilot customers across different lanes.
Mapping matrix linking signal combinations to onboarding lane decisions exists and is approved by Growth and Support leadership.
Console view prototype surfaced to Product Console team that shows queued private deploy requests by lane and estimated TTR.
Runbooks and minimal preflight probe scripts committed to GitHub referenced in intake responses for Concierge and Escalation lanes.
SLA expectations for each lane are documented (expected lead time, SOW triggers) and shared with Sales/CS.
Telemetry: instrumented metrics for conversion rate from intake -> completed onboarding, and median time per lane captured on the onboarding dashboard.
steps: Week 1: Stakeholder alignment (Sales, SE, SRE, Legal) and schema surface workshop.
Week 2: Draft intake schema and intake form + proto Console wireframe.
Week 3: Implement preflight probes (network port checks, egress validation, proxy fingerprint) and sample runbooks.
Week 4: Pilot with 3 customers (one self-serve candidate, one concierge, one escalation), capture feedback.
Week 5: Iterate and finalize mapping matrix; brief GTM and Support; publish docs and enable routing rules.
Week 6: Dashboard rollout and instrumentation for metrics; retro and next steps planning.
risks: Risk: Over-simplification of signals could misclassify high-risk customers into self-serve lane. Mitigation: require a minimum preflight pass for self-serve and tie over-ride to SE review.
Risk: Preflight probes may be blocked by customer firewalls. Mitigation: provide optional offline checklists and SE-assisted remote probe options.
Risk: Console UI changes require coordination with Console team release calendar. Mitigation: implement intake-first API and defer full Console integration to v2 if needed.
